Blood–Brain Barrier Microrobotic Sampling and Quantum Neurobiomarker Sensing at the Limit An integrity-first research architecture for localized neural-microenvironment evidence Core coupling Blood–brain barrier models × neural microenvironment sampling × quantum biomarker readout Research scale 30 linked derivations × 82 chapters × 410 single-page research sections × 200 detailed Research Gates Main result A testable architecture that makes preserved barrier and neural function prerequisites for interpreting localized neurobiomarker evidence. Mother lineage Microrobotic Sampling and Quantum Biosensing Co-Design at the Limit Publication Abstract This monograph asks whether microrobotic systems can obtain position-traceable, extremely low-volume samples near a blood–brain barrier model and reveal local neuroinflammatory, metabolic, ionic, proteolytic, or extracellular-vesicle states without opening the barrier or changing neural function. The scientific object is the complete chain linking neurovascular-unit state, flow, probe pose, contact force, sample volume, adsorption, biomarker recovery, quantum and classical readout, barrier integrity, neural function, and inference. Local signal strength alone is not evidence of preserved sampling. The framework treats inflammation, metabolic stress, barrier leak, and operation-induced injury as competing explanations. Its central falsifiable proposition is that localized sampling should increase independently verified information under a matched disturbance budget while transendothelial resistance, size-selective permeability, junction organization, and neural electrophysiology remain within preregistered limits. If sampling damage cannot be separated from target biology, if the quantum channel does not beat a strong classical comparator after overhead, or if sample provenance breaks, the appropriate decision is abstention or stop. Scientific Position and Hard Boundary Validation begins with blood–brain barrier chips, vascularized neural organoids, induced-pluripotent-stem-cell models, ex vivo tissues, and separately governed preclinical systems. None of these models alone establishes human diagnostic performance, therapeutic benefit, or safe autonomous in-body operation. TEER is not allowed to substitute for permeability, morphology, viability, and neural function; a quantum resource is not allowed to substitute for molecular selectivity or an independent reference method. Candidate Research Expression NBBB = Ineuro Pintegrity Plocalization − λb ΔBbarrier − λs Dshear − λi Hinference • Ineuro measures independently verified new information about the local neural microenvironment. • Pintegrity measures preservation of molecular, cellular, barrier, and neural-function states. • Plocalization measures confidence in the sample's physical and temporal origin. • ΔBbarrier measures changes in resistance, permeability, junction state, and recovery. • Dshear measures mechanical and fluidic injury caused by approach, contact, flow, and sampling. • Hinference measures the risk of extrapolating from the chosen model to unsupported biological or clinical claims. Authorization, persistent barrier damage, altered neural activity, failed sterility, lost sample identity, missing raw evidence, and failed independent references are hard vetoes. No favorable weighted score can cancel them. Five-Layer Research Architecture 01 Barrier and Claim Contract Declare the BBB model, target state, evidence tier, integrity limits, baseline, and hard vetoes. 02 Sampling Physics and Provenance Measure pose, route, flow, force, volume, depletion, adsorption, carryover, recovery, and residual burden. 03 Quantum and Classical Metrology Preserve raw spin, photon, spectral, thermal, field, and classical channels with calibration ancestry and joint covariance. 04 Injury–Disease Discrimination Use mechanical, optical, thermal, and inflammatory shams plus delayed recovery, electrophysiology, histology, and analytical chemistry. 05 External Rebuild and Exit Repeat across models and sites, reconstruct without the creator, and permit abstention, simplification, or retirement. Minimum Verifiable Prototype Create a blinded BBB-on-chip containing local inflammatory and metabolic gradients plus matched regions in which contact or flow produces similar biomarker changes. Compare fixed outlet sampling, calibrated manual microprobes, and bounded microrobotic sampling under equal sample-volume, energy, optical-dose, time, and analysis budgets. Freeze the sampling policy and predicted gradient before revealing the challenge key. Orthogonal resistance, tracer permeability, junction imaging, electrophysiology, histology, and analytical chemistry then decide whether the system detected target biology, induced injury, memorized position, or should abstain. Research Contributions • Makes preserved barrier and neural function prerequisites for interpreting any localized biomarker gain. • Treats microrobotic sampling as a physical intervention with measurable flow, force, depletion, adsorption, carryover, and delayed effects. • Requires quantum readout to compete against fit-for-purpose classical methods after preparation, calibration, optical, thermal, and computational costs are counted. • Connects thirty physical, transport, metrological, statistical, and governance derivations to chapter and Research Gate corridors. • Separates neuroinflammation, metabolic stress, junction failure, and mechanical injury through explicit competing models and matched shams. • Turns two hundred Research Gates into detailed future-study cards containing a baseline, minimum test, evidence packet, competing explanation, stop condition, next path, and successor invitation. • Preserves abstention, negative results, model-specific validity, and successor-controlled retirement as first-class scientific outcomes. What the Book Does Not Claim The monograph does not report a completed human trial, validate a clinical diagnostic device, or authorize autonomous sampling inside the human brain. Barrier chips and organoids reproduce selected functions rather than the full human neurovascular unit. Biomarker changes cannot by themselves establish a neurodegenerative diagnosis, and a sensitive quantum channel cannot by itself identify a molecule. Translation requires separate biological, engineering, ethical, regulatory, clinical, and post-deployment programs.
